 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.
 Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Luka Dončić accumulated 37 points (12-of-27 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal, two blocks and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Warriors. 
 Dončić was rolling during the first quarter, knocking down five three-pointers and scoring 21 points. Unfortunately for the Lakers, their star guard needed a rest to start the second quarter, which opened the door for the Warriors to turn things around. While Dončić scored 13 second-half points, he didn’t get enough help from teammates beyond Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler to avoid the defeat. The Lakers host Toronto on Sunday to end their week.

 Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 While Dončić is back after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Clippers, Ziaire Williams will miss another game. As a result, LaRavia will remain in the starting lineup, while Dončić’s return pushes Quentin Grimes to the bench.

 Dončić missed Wednesday’s game against the Clippers, which came on the second night of a back-to-back. He’ll be back to his usual spot in the starting lineup, which will likely push Quentin Grimes back to the bench following a productive spot start.

 Dončić will miss the second leg of the Lakers’ back-to-back, which means Austin Reaves should be the focal point of the offense. Quentin Grimes or Collin Sexton will likely replace Dončić in the starting unit, with both taking on extended roles. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić amassed 41 points (12-of-22 FGs, 11-of-13 Fts), five rebounds, nine assists, one block and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 One game removed from dropping 52 points on the Jazz, Dončić had another prolific scoring night on Tuesday. In addition to the high field-goal percentage, he kept the turnovers in check, committing only two. Despite averaging nearly six turnovers per game, Dončić has been one of the most valuable players in nine-cat formats. Shooting 87.5 percent from the foul line, which represents significant improvement, certainly helps. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Jazz with 52 points (17-of-30 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and eight three-pointers. 
 Dončić put on a show in Salt Lake City, recording his first 50-point game of the new season. And he was highly efficient, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. The only thing that could have made Sunday better for managers rostering Dončić was getting the two rebounds he needed to finish with a triple-double. The Lakers play four games in Week 2, starting Tuesday against the Trail Blazers.

 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić tallied 23 points (8-of-21 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers. 
 After an excellent start to his 2026-27 season against the Warriors on Wednesday, Dončić had some efficiency issues on Friday. While category league managers won’t be too concerned with the percentages, the Lakers’ point guard racked up a career-high 11 turnovers. By now, many managers rostering Dončić are fine with punting that category, but it’s still a startling number for him. He’ll look to put together a better showing when the Lakers visit the Jazz on Sunday.

 Luka had fun going at Yaxel all game and put up his usual monster stat line. Luka seems like a lock to finish top 4 of fantasy leagues, and if you drafted him, you’re feeling very happy about your selection. You’re just hoping that the turnovers stay low, and he hits his free throws.

 Luka Dončić dropped 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Nuggets. 
 While Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler both played 31 minutes in Friday’s preseason finale, Dončić played 19 minutes. However, that was the plan, with the Lakers holding their star point guard out for the entire second half. Like Reaves, Dončić will now carry an even heavier workload with LeBron James out of the picture. Even with turnover concerns, Luka will be one of the best fantasy players, regardless of league format. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić recorded 23 points (6-of-16 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Thursday’s exhibition against the Kings. 
 Dončić picked up a technical foul during the third quarter of Thursday’s exhibition, but this is a good time for that to happen since they don’t carry over into the regular season. Dončić led the Lakers in points and shot attempts, and that will once again be the norm when the regular season begins. Currently boasting a top-5 ADP, Luka’s fantasy ceiling rises slightly in turnover-punt builds.

 Immanuel Quickley accounted for 12 points (3-of-13 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Quickley has made at least three three-pointers in four straight and five of six games this season. That, along with the rebounds and assists, was the positive from his performance on Sunday. However, Quickley shot poorly against the Lakers, dropping his field-goal percentage to 37.6 percent for the season. It certainly isn’t impossible for a guard to provide solid value despite a low field-goal percentage, but fantasy managers want to see Quickley shoot better than he has.

 RJ Barrett accumulated 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), 10 rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Barrett has scored at least 20 points in three of his last four games, a stretch that coincides with the Raptors’ loss of Kawhi Leonard to a knee injury. While he didn’t record any defensive stats on Sunday, fantasy managers will be pleased with Barrett’s double-double, his first of the season, and the assists. The Raptors play three games next week, starting with the Clippers on Monday.

 Scottie Barnes finished Sunday’s loss to the Lakers with 29 points (11-of-20 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and two steals.
 Barnes’ mid-range mastery helped him score 29 points, and he’s scored at least 28 in three straight and four of his last five games. The exception was the October 25 loss to the Timberwolves, in which the Raptors’ star went scoreless. With Kawhi Leonard (knee) out for a few weeks, Barnes will need to shoulder more responsibility on both ends of the floor. And he’s shown the ability to do that in the past.

 Walker Kessler amassed 16 points (6-of-6 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 15 rebounds, one assist, one steal and three blocks in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
 A favorite of many fantasy managers willing to punt free-throw percentage, Kessler didn’t miss a shot from the field or the foul line on Sunday. Add in the rebounds and blocks, and this was a nice end to the week for those rostering the 7-footer. Kessler, who’s averaging just under three blocks per game, has blocked at least three shots in three games.

 Kris Dunn accumulated 12 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and seven steals in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
 After failing to record a steal in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves, Dunn compensated with the best performance of his career. The seven steals mark a new career high for the former lottery pick, whose defense has made him a fixture in Tyronn Lue’s rotation since he joined the Clippers in 2024-25. Dunn also shot well on Sunday, but his defensive potential makes him an intriguing option for managers in 12-team leagues seeking steals.

 Kobe Sanders amassed 16 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Sanders had his most productive game of the season so far, setting new highs in points and three-pointers. He’s now played at least 20 minutes in four straight games, logging 30 against the Warriors. Sunday’s performance isn’t enough to get him on the radar in most fantasy leagues, but it may ensure Sanders a place in head coach Tyronn Lue’s rotation while the Clippers await the returns of Brandon Ingram and Max Strus.
